title: Capacity Safeguard Dashboard: operator controls and change timeline
creator: Ariana Patel
description:
Goal: Ship a single Console surface for operators to confidently set throughput guarantees, configure autoscaling policies, and review a tamper-proof change timeline for Dedicated fleets. This ticket scopes the UX and product requirements for the Capacity Safeguard Dashboard (operator-facing) and defines the rollout strategy for gradual enablement in Dedicated clusters.

Background: Customers running Dedicated pools need clear controls that balance guaranteed throughput, cost commitments, and safe defaults for autoscaling. Current Console fragments (presets, manual controls, and audit history) are scattered; operators ask for a unified place to make changes, validate impact, and reason about customer-visible guarantees.

What we will deliver in this ticket: 1) An operator panel that exposes: a throughput target slider (rps/throughput tokens), min/max pool limits, burst window and burst budget, policy presets (latency-first, cost-first, aggressive-burst), and a quick-simulate mode to preview expected P95 latency and cost delta for next 24h. 2) Autoscaling policy editor where a policy can be based on avg latency, token consumption, or queue depth, with cooldowns and emergency cap. 3) Immutable change timeline with per-change diff, author, timestamp, and optional justification that is surfaced in the Logs and exportable (CSV). 4) Alerting hook to tie policy changes to ops runbooks and SRE notification channels. 5) Role-based access control flags (enable/disable edit) surface for Private customers.

Non-functional requirements: Dashboard must load initial payload under 700ms for fleets < 200 nodes; change writes must be acknowledged within 300ms and persisted to audit store before returning success. All writes must generate an immutable audit event with human-readable diff and link to the affected fleet config.

Trade-offs considered: - Inline advanced policy editing vs. guided wizard: we ship a compact guided wizard first and hide advanced JSON editor behind an "Advanced" toggle to reduce risk. - Strong defaults vs. strict safety: default policies are conservative to avoid unintended cost shocks; operators can opt into aggressive presets.

Rollout plan: 1) Alpha behind feature flag for internal SRE and two pilot customers (2 weeks) 2) Beta for all Dedicated customers with "opt-in" toggle (4 weeks) 3) GA with enforced RBAC and exportable audit logs (console-2026.03).

Monitoring & success metrics: - Reduction in manual intervention incidents during traffic spikes by 30% within 8 weeks of GA - Average time to recover from overloaded node < 5 minutes when using recommended presets - 95% of policy change flows completed without helpdesk contact in pilot cohort
acceptance_criteria:
1) Operators can set throughput target and min/max pool and save changes; saved change creates an immutable audit event containing diff, author, timestamp, and justification.
2) Autoscaling policy editor supports policy by latency, token consumption, and queue depth; cooldowns respected and shown in UI.
3) Quick-simulate returns expected P95 latency and cost delta within 10% of runtime simulator for pilot traffic.
4) RBAC settings prevent non-admin from applying changes when role is read-only.
5) Dashboard loads in < 700ms for fleets < 200 nodes in internal performance tests.
6) All change events are exportable as CSV and visible in Console change history view.
